# std/prelude

Imported into every program automatically (`--no-prelude` turns it off): the `Error`
interface, `Unit`, and the error types that `?` and `.context()` build. It also imports
[`std/string`](string)'s ASCII helpers, which is why those need no import.

## API reference

### `Error`

```milo
pub interface Error
```

The structural error interface. Any type with `message(self: &Self): string`
satisfies it, so a fn can return `Result<T, Heap<Error>>` and `?` boxes whatever
error a callee produced (a struct, an enum, or a plain `string`, which arrives as a
`ErrorMessage`). The message is the one thing every error owes its reader; the concrete
type is still there behind the box for a caller that wants to look.

### `ErrorContext`

```milo
pub struct ErrorContext
```

What `r.context("reading config")` wraps an error in: the note, then the cause it
was raised for, so the message reads outermost first ("reading config: not found:
x.toml"). The cause is any boxed Error, so a chain nests as deep as the call stack
that annotated it.

Fields: `note: string`, `cause: Heap<Error>`.

#### `ErrorContext.message`

```milo
fn ErrorContext.message(self: &ErrorContext): string
```

The note, a colon, and the cause's own message.

### `ErrorMessage`

```milo
pub struct ErrorMessage
```

A `string` error boxed as an `Error`: what `?` makes of a `Result<T, string>` in a
fn that returns `Result<T, Heap<Error>>`.

Fields: `text: string`.

#### `ErrorMessage.message`

```milo
fn ErrorMessage.message(self: &ErrorMessage): string
```

The string the error was raised with.

### `Unit`

```milo
pub struct Unit
```

The single success value for operations that return no data. Use
Result&lt;Unit, E> for fallible commands; `void` is a function return type, not a
value that can inhabit Result.
